description: A video from April 12, taken by a passenger on board the MV Hondius, the hantavirus-hit cruise ship, shows the ship’s captain announcing the death of someone on board the previous day. Captain Jan Dobrogowski says the death is believed to be due to “natural causes.” Oceanwide Expeditions, the ship’s operator, said in a statement, “At the time of the announcement, the cause of death of this individual was unknown.” At the time of publication, the cause still wasn’t confirmed to be hantavirus.

author: CNN
description:
The World Health Organization said Thursday that five confirmed infections have been identified among people connected to the cruise ship MV Hondius, as health authorities across several countries race to trace and contain the outbreak.

Three people – a Dutch couple and a German national – have died since the vessel departed Argentina last month. The first suspected case was a 70-year-old Dutchman, who suddenly fell ill on the ship with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea, South Africa’s Health Department told CNN. He died on board on April 11.

Iran has laid out a set of new rules for ships seeking to cross the Strait of Hormuz, according to a document seen by CNN, as Tehran seeks to cement control over the international waterway.

Iran’s president said he had a lengthy meeting with the country’s new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, according to Iranian media, marking the first reported in-person talks between a top Iranian official and Khamenei. Oil prices are falling today after a roller-coaster ride this week. US gas prices remain at $4.50. Meanwhile, energy giant Shell has reported a $1.3 billion jump in profits.
